module.title: Business intelligence and semantic delivery
module.summary: Design a dashboard backward from the decision it serves, label and bind every number to a metric contract, separate page permissions from data privileges, communicate freshness, define metrics once in a metric view, and compare the native AI/BI page with Power BI, Tableau and driver-based clients, ending in a storyboard and an acceptance script.
objectives: Write a decision chain and defensible, contract-bound labels for a morning quality page.
Write an access matrix and freshness statement that separate page permissions, the publish-time data-permission choice and table privileges, and order the refresh after the job.
Compare AI/BI, metric views, Genie One, Power BI, Tableau and ODBC or JDBC clients, and write a storyboard and an acceptance script with independent expected values.

scenarios.title: Deliver Cinderline's morning quality page
scenarios.context: Fictional Cinderline Components runs a North plant with four lines. Supervisors meet at 8 a.m. to choose which line to investigate first and today argue over two printed reports. The metric contract for unit_defect_rate version 1 is proposed; a nightly job publishes accepted inspections and a publish-run table, normally by 02:10 but occasionally not until after the meeting. The operations director asks the data team to "connect Power BI and build a dashboard" for the meeting, and the finance team already uses Power BI.
scenarios.task: Produce the delivery plan the operations director signs before anything is built: a storyboard of the meeting, the metric definitions the page reads, an access matrix for the page and its underlying data, the refresh and freshness design, an acceptance script with exact expected values and signers, and a short recommendation on where Power BI fits, with explicit unknowns.
requirements: Storyboard frames that each name time, actor, surface, what is read and what is decided, including the late-job morning.
Metric definitions bound to the contract by name and version, with the plant ratio of sums, the empty cases and the restatement mark.
An access matrix separating page permissions, the publish-time data-permission choice and table privileges, with the identity that writes the data kept apart from the page.
A refresh ordered after the job and a freshness statement in words for the normal and not-updated states.
An acceptance script whose expected values come from outside the page, with identity rows and signers, and a Power BI recommendation that says what does not travel.
scenarios.model:
### Storyboard
Five frames plus the late-morning variant. 07:30, plant analyst in the workspace: reads the freshness line and the four tiles against the reconciliation sheet. 07:45, supervisors on phones through Genie One: read "Covers Tuesday. Published 06:32. Restated days are marked." first. 07:47: compare four line tiles, choose line 2 at 6.0% first. 07:50: see line 2's day-2 mark, 5.1% with previous 5.3%, and accept it. 08:05, quality lead: opens the excluded inspection through the quarantine link. Late variant: frame 2 reads "Not updated: showing Monday. See the operator note." and frame 3 becomes a decision to use Monday knowingly.

### Metric definitions
`unit_defect_rate` v1 from the metric contract, held as a measure in a metric view: try_divide(SUM(defective_units), SUM(inspected_units)) over accepted inspections, dimensions line_id and business_day; the plant figure is the same measure with no line grouping, never a mean of line rates. Beside each tile: accepted, excluded and quarantined counts. Empty cases render "no inspections" or "no inspected units". Restated days carry a flag and the previous value. The freshness tile reads the latest successful publish-run row.

### Access matrix
The page is published with individual data permissions, so each viewer's own grants protect the rows. north-reporting-analysts: Can View; SELECT on accepted.daily_line_rate; must not reach raw or quarantine rows through any filter. quality-stewards: Can View and the quarantine link; SELECT on accepted and quarantine tables; must not edit. Data team (page owner): Can Edit, working with its own grants and never those of sp-north-nightly, the principal that writes the accepted tables and holds no page permission. Everyone else: nothing on either door. Rejected alternative: shared data permissions from a personal login, which would hand every viewer the author's reach.

### Refresh and freshness
A dashboard task follows the nightly publishing task; if the job has not published by 7:30 the freshness line says so and the operator and analyst are notified.

### Acceptance script
From the five-day reconciliation sheet: line 3, day 4 = 4.8%; line 2, day 2 counts 20 / 1 / 1 (accepted, excluded, quarantined); line 2's day-2 mark with previous 5.3% after the day-4 correction; line 4, day 5 = "no inspections"; line filter 3 leaves the plant at 4.5%; the late-morning simulation shows the not-updated sentence; test analyst sees tiles and is refused the quarantine link; outsider cannot load. Signers: plant analyst (values), quality lead (counts and marks), security lead (access).

### External BI
The finance team's Power BI request is a second page: its own connection identity with SELECT on the accepted view, DirectQuery on a SQL warehouse or an Import copy whose sharing Power BI governs, the measure read from the metric view by SQL, its own freshness caption and its own acceptance row. Nothing of the AI/BI page travels.

### Unknowns
Consumer access for the supervisors' group, phone rendering at 390 pixels, and whether supervisors act on the page, which the pilot readout must observe.
scenarios.reasoning: The plan answers the director's request by the decision the meeting makes rather than by a tool: every tile traces to the contract, the matrix keeps the two doors and the data-permission choice explicit, freshness is designed for the late morning, and the acceptance script is the evidence. Power BI is treated as a second page with its own identity, freshness and acceptance, so the request is met without pretending the page's controls follow the data into another tool.

rubric.weak: A list of charts or screenshots with no audience or decision.
rubric.partial: Audience and decision named, but frames do not say what is read or omit the late-job morning.
rubric.strong: Frames name time, actor, surface, sentence read and decision, including the not-updated variant, and each maps to an acceptance row.

rubric.weak: Tiles labelled "Defect rate" with a plant average of line rates.
rubric.partial: Contract named but the empty case or restatement mark is missing, or labels lack period or denominator.
rubric.strong: Every tile bound to unit_defect_rate v1, plant as ratio of sums, empty cases in words, restatement mark and exclusion counts shown.

rubric.weak: "Share with the supervisors"; refresh on a clock with a timestamp in the corner.
rubric.partial: Page and table grants listed, but the data-permission choice is unstated, or freshness says only a time.
rubric.strong: Two doors per principal, individual data permissions so the grants protect the rows, the writing principal kept off the page, refresh after the job, and freshness in words for both states.

rubric.weak: "Check that it looks right"; Power BI assumed to inherit the page.
rubric.partial: Expected values given but copied from the page, or no identity rows; Power BI mentioned without its own controls.
rubric.strong: Independent expected values, filter, empty, restated, late and identity rows with signers; Power BI given its own identity, freshness and acceptance, with unknowns listed.

disclosures.question: Does the finance team's Power BI report have to show the same numbers as the page?
disclosures.response: Yes, to one decimal, on the same business day. Finance is willing to read from a view or metric view the data team owns, but its report is shared through its own Power BI workspace.

disclosures.question: Do supervisors have consumer access today?
disclosures.response: Unknown. The workspace administrator has not confirmed which groups hold the entitlement; until they do, the phone path is listed as unverified.

claims.description: AI/BI dashboards are low-code dashboards built from datasets; each dataset is based on a table, view, metric view or custom SQL query, every visualization reads from one or more datasets, and a published dashboard can be shared with users registered to the Databricks account.
claims.context: AI/BI dashboards on Databricks; features and limits vary by release.

claims.description: Field filters narrow results by dataset fields and come as single value, multiple values, date picker, date range picker, text entry and range slider; for relatively small datasets they are often applied in the browser without re-running the query.

Dashboard parameters substitute values into dataset queries at runtime so data is filtered before aggregation; parameter filters come as single value, multiple values, date picker and date range, and query-based parameters draw their allowed values from a dataset.
claims.context: AI/BI dashboard parameters; syntax on the current page.

claims.description: An AI/BI dashboard has its own permission levels, Can View (CAN_READ), Can Run, Can Edit and Can Manage, which govern the dashboard object; whether its queries return data is decided separately by data permissions on the underlying objects.
claims.context: Workspace object ACLs; Unity Catalog privileges are a separate system.

claims.description: At publish time the publisher chooses shared data permissions (the default), where viewers' queries run with the publisher's data permissions and share one cache, or individual data permissions, where each viewer's own credentials and access to the data decide the results and the cache is per user.
claims.context: Publishing AI/BI dashboards; defaults may change.

claims.description: The dashboard API publishes with embed_credentials; publishing as a service principal needs at least CAN MANAGE on the dashboard, SELECT on its data sources and CAN USE on the warehouse, after which viewers use the principal's permissions and audit logs show the principal as the executor.

A dashboard schedule runs all dataset SQL on a periodic cadence and, for a dashboard published with shared data permissions, refreshes the shared cache; subscriptions send snapshots by email, Slack or Microsoft Teams.
claims.context: Published AI/BI dashboards; each run uses warehouse compute.

claims.description: A dashboard task in a job refreshes a dashboard and sends a snapshot to its own subscriber list, using a serverless or pro SQL warehouse.
claims.context: Lakeflow Jobs task types; availability varies.

claims.description: A Unity Catalog metric view separates measure definitions from dimensions, is defined in YAML and registered with SQL DDL or Catalog Explorer, lets a query group by any available dimension while the engine generates the computation, and is queried with the MEASURE function.
claims.context: Unity Catalog semantics; status and runtime requirements on the current page.

claims.description: Databricks AI/BI comprises dashboards for visualization and reporting and, under Genie One, Genie Agents for conversational analytics configured by data teams with trusted data, metrics and business rules.
claims.context: Product family naming as of September 2026.

claims.description: Genie One, previously Databricks One, is the simplified interface where business users view AI/BI dashboards, ask questions in natural language and use Databricks Apps; the consumer access entitlement directs users there and is the least-privileged option.
claims.context: Workspace-level Genie One; entitlements administered per workspace.

claims.description: Power BI connects to Databricks from Power BI Desktop through Partner Connect, a manual hostname and HTTP path connection or the Delta Sharing connector; the connector supports ADBC, Import and DirectQuery, with SQL warehouses recommended for DirectQuery; data can also be published to the Power BI service and semantic model refreshes orchestrated with a Power BI task.
claims.context: Power BI integration; licence and tenant settings are Power BI's.

claims.description: Tableau Desktop connects through Partner Connect or manually, and with Tableau Cloud data sources can be created from Unity Catalog tables or schemas directly from the Databricks UI.
claims.context: Tableau integration; Tableau-side permissions are Tableau's.

claims.description: Databricks provides ODBC and JDBC drivers for tools and clients; some tools need the ODBC driver installed, such as Tableau Desktop, while recent Power BI Desktop releases include it.

AI/BI dashboards keep a best-effort 24-hour result cache: shared across viewers for a dashboard published with shared data permissions, per user for drafts and individual data permissions, and populated by scheduled updates.
claims.context: Dashboard caching behaviour; best effort, not a guarantee.

claims.description: A published AI/BI dashboard can be shared with users registered to the Databricks account who lack workspace access; such users are limited to Can Run whatever level the sharing dialog shows.

Embedding for external users places a dashboard in an external application for viewers without Databricks accounts, using a service principal with read access to the dashboard and its data and one-hour tokens scoped to each viewer.
claims.context: External embedding; availability checked on the current page.

claims.description: A published dashboard stores its field filter and parameter selections in the URL, so a bookmarked or shared link reopens the dashboard with those values applied.

concepts.definition: The audience, decision, action and metric a dashboard exists to serve, written before any tile is drawn.
A tile label carrying axis treatment, units, period, denominator and publish time.
Tying each tile to a named, versioned metric contract whose grain, denominator and empty rule it inherits.
Two dashboard controls: a field filter narrows returned rows, a parameter is substituted into the SQL before aggregation.
An access level on the dashboard object, separate from privileges on the tables its queries read.
The publish-time choice of whether viewers' queries run with the publisher's data permissions or their own.
Words on the page naming the period covered, the publish time, restatements and the not-updated state, read from a run table.
A Unity Catalog object holding measures separately from dimensions so a ratio is recomputed over sums at every grouping.
The business-user surface for AI/BI dashboards and the least-privileged entitlement that admits users to it.
A separate BI tool reading Databricks through a connector or driver under its own identity, sharing and refresh.
The meeting drawn as frames naming time, actor, surface, what is read, what is decided and where next.
Checks with expected values from outside the page, the states and identities to try, and a signer per row.
